# PCD-9784 Docs Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Every registry page that imports by a server-generated ID says how to look the ID up, and the registry carries a lab-validated, runnable zero-to-VM example for Community Edition; a handoff file lets the pcd-doc-writer agent make the matching first-party edits.

**Architecture:** Registry docs are generated by tfplugindocs from schema descriptions, `examples/`, and `templates/` (`make generate`), so every change lands in those sources and the generated `docs/` tree is committed. Two new guides live in `templates/guides/`; the Community Edition guide pulls its HCL from a runnable `examples/complete/community-edition/` directory with `tffile` so text and code cannot drift. The first-party page is not edited here; a handoff Markdown file outside the repo drives the pcd-doc-writer agent.

**Tech Stack:** terraform-plugin-docs (`make generate`), Terraform 1.15 with a dev override of the provider built from this worktree, the CE lab reached through the `pcd.pf9.io` tunnel, the sibling `pcd-tf-testsuite` credential loader (never type the lab password), `pcdctl` on the lab hypervisor for command validation.

## Global Constraints

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-pcd-9784-docs-design.md`. Decisions there are final: `pcdctl` verb in registry docs with one "`openstack` works too" note; full lab run with NFS; docs-only release `v0.1.11` after merge; adjacent fixes included.
- American English everywhere (behavior, authorize, initialize).
- No Claude attribution in commits or PR text. Branch is `pushkar/pcd-9784-docs` (already renamed).
- Never put the lab password on a command line, in a file under the repo, or in the handoff. Reach the lab through `scratchpad/osc.py`, `scratchpad/tf.py`, `scratchpad/pcdctl_remote2.py` (they load credentials from the testsuite).
- The registry ignores `docs/superpowers/`; `docs/index.md`, `docs/resources/`, `docs/data-sources/`, `docs/guides/` are generated and must be regenerated, never hand-edited.
- Before the PR: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l internal/` clean, `golangci-lint run ./...` 0 issues, `make generate` with no diff afterwards, `terraform fmt -check -recursive examples/`.
- Lab-verified commands to cite (see spec "Verified facts"): `pcdctl volume type list`, `pcdctl volume type show <name> -f value -c id`, `pcdctl hypervisor show <hypervisor-id> -c service_host`, `pcdctl compute service list --service nova-compute -c Host -c Zone`, `pcdctl token issue -f value -c id`, resmgr paths `/resmgr/v1/hosts`, `/resmgr/v2/hostconfigs`, `/resmgr/v2/blueprint`, `/resmgr/v2/clusters`, and `/etc/pf9/host_id.conf`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the guide template**

`templates/guides/importing.md.tmpl` with this front matter and sections. Headings are the contract; prose may be tightened.

```markdown
---
page_title: "Importing existing resources - PCD Provider"
subcategory: ""
description: |-
  How to bring resources that already exist in PCD under Terraform management, and where to find the IDs import needs.
---

# Importing existing resources

## When you import
(one blueprint per region; existing volume types, networks, images; the choice is import, not recreate)

## Set up the CLI
- pcdctl install pointer (docs.platform9.com PCD CLI page), RC file from **Settings > API Access**, `source pcdctlrc`
- Community Edition: `export OS_INSECURE=true` before any command (self-signed certificate)
- Note: every `pcdctl` command below is the OpenStack CLI command with the verb swapped; `openstack ...` works identically with the same RC file.

## Two ways to import
### terraform import (you write the HCL first) — volume type example ending in an empty plan
### Import blocks with generated configuration (Terraform 1.5+) — import {} + `terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf`; sensitive attributes come out as `null # sensitive`; for the blueprint that is exactly right (backends are read from the server and preserved)

## Finding IDs
### Block storage / Compute / Networking / Images / Identity / Load balancer / DNS / Key manager — one table each: Resource | Import ID | Where to find it
### PCD-native resources (resmgr)
- host UUID: three ways (hypervisor show service_host; compute service list; /etc/pf9/host_id.conf) and which work before the host has roles
- host configuration ID, blueprint name, cluster name: token + curl the resmgr paths; cluster name also in `pcdctl aggregate list`

## Worked example: the region's cluster blueprint
```

```shell
TOKEN=$(pcdctl token issue -f value -c id)

```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the example**

`provider.tf`:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    pcd = {
      source  = "platform9/pcd"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

# Credentials come from the RC file downloaded from Settings > API Access:
#   source pcdctlrc   (OS_AUTH_URL, OS_USERNAME, OS_PASSWORD, OS_PROJECT_NAME, OS_REGION_NAME, ...)
provider "pcd" {
  # Community Edition ships a self-signed certificate.
  insecure = true
}
```

`variables.tf`: `host_id` (string, the resmgr host UUID, with the lookup in the description), `host_interface` (string, default `"enp1s0"`), `nfs_export` (string, `"<server-ip>:/exported/path"`), `network_cidr`, `network_gateway`, `allocation_pool_start`, `allocation_pool_end` (strings, required), `dns_nameservers` (list(string), default `["8.8.8.8"]`), `region_name` (default `"region-1"`), `cluster_name` (default `"cluster-1"`), `dns_domain_name` (default `"pcd.local."`).

`region.tf` (order matters and is the guide's narrative):

```terraform
# 1. A volume type: what tenants ask for when they create a volume. Its
#    volume_backend_name must match a backend declared in the blueprint below.
resource "pcd_blockstorage_volume_type" "nfs" {
  name        = "nfs"
  description = "NFS-backed persistent storage"
  is_public   = true
  extra_specs = { volume_backend_name = "nfs" }
}

# 2. The region's single cluster blueprint. storage_backends_json declares the
#    Persistent Storage backends; the keys of the NFS driver are the ones the
#    PCD UI offers under Add Volume Backend Configuration > NFS.
resource "pcd_cluster_blueprint" "region" {
  name            = var.region_name
  dns_domain_name = var.dns_domain_name

  virtual_networking = {
    enabled       = true
    underlay_type = "vlan"
    vnid_range    = "1000:2000"
  }

  image_library_storage        = pcd_blockstorage_volume_type.nfs.name
  image_library_shared_storage = true
  instance_shared_storage      = false
  vm_storage                   = "/opt/data/instances"

  storage_backends_json = jsonencode({
    nfs = {
      nfs = {
        driver = "NFS"
        config = {
          nfs_shares_config           = "/opt/pf9/etc/pf9-cindervolume-base/conf.d/nfs_shares"
          nfs_mount_points            = var.nfs_export
          nfs_mount_point_base        = "/opt/pf9/etc/pf9-cindervolume-base/volumes/"
          nfs_snapshot_support        = "true"
          nas_secure_file_permissions = "false"
          nas_secure_file_operations  = "false"
        }
      }
    }
  })
}
```

then `pcd_host_config`, `pcd_host_config_assignment`, `pcd_cluster` (HA on, rebalancing on), and three `pcd_host_cluster_role` resources (`hypervisor` with `host_cluster`, `image-library`, `persistent-storage` with `backends = ["nfs"]`), all with `wait_until_converged = true` and `depends_on = [pcd_host_config_assignment.host1]`.

`platform.tf`: flat provider network on `physnet1` (`depends_on` the hypervisor role), subnet from the variables, security group with SSH and ICMP rules, CirrOS image (`image_source_url = "https://download.cirros-cloud.net/0.6.2/cirros-0.6.2-x86_64-disk.img"`, `depends_on` the image-library role), flavor 1 vCPU / 512 MB / 5 GB.

`app.tf`: instance on the network (`depends_on` the subnet), 1 GB volume of type `nfs` (`depends_on` the storage role), attachment. `outputs.tf`: `instance_ip`, `instance_id`, `volume_id`, `host_config_id`.

`terraform.tfvars.example`: every required variable with a placeholder value and a comment. `README.md`: three paragraphs (what it builds, how to run, how to destroy) pointing at the guide.

## Execution notes (2026-09-04)

Tasks 1 to 6 are done; Task 7 waits for the merge decision. What the lab run changed
relative to the plan:

- The first apply stalled: with `backends = ["nfs"]` (the top-level key) resmgr computed an
  empty backend set, `cinder-volume` could not start, and the host looped in
  `auth-converging`, where resmgr refuses every role change (409). Terraform was
  interrupted; the tainted storage role was replaced with `backends = ["nfs-primary"]`
  (resmgr accepted the removal after 51 s), which produced the correct settings. The
  `backends` description, both examples, the guide, and the handoff were corrected.
- Convergence then still failed silently because the NFS options were quoted strings
  (`"true"`); the host agent reads them back as booleans. Unquoting them in the blueprint
  (an in-place `pcd_cluster_blueprint` update) made the host reach `ok` within a minute.
  Documented in the guide, both examples, the blueprint description, and the handoff.
- `terraform untaint` was needed on the three roles after the interrupted apply so the
  full apply added only the six remaining resources (network, subnet, image, instance,
  volume, attachment): image 1m21s, instance 1m31s, volume 3s, attachment 9s; VM
  pingable at 172.16.122.11; plan clean.
- Teardown took three `terraform destroy` runs: 422 on the storage role (the deleted
  image's backing volume `image-<id>` stays behind; deleted by hand), 500 on the cluster
  and 403 `HostInAuthState` on the host-config unassignment while deauthorizations
  landed. Recorded in the guide's Destroy section and the example README.
- The image endpoint needs no override for LAN users: the provider already prefers the
  image-library host's admin endpoint (`https://<host>:9494`); the guide states the
  reachability requirement instead.
- Lab left as the testsuite expects: host `136fc11a` authorized with no roles, region
  empty, host NIC restored, cinder pre-enabled; the NFS export on the hypervisor VM
  (`/srv/nfs/pcd`) remains and is harmless.
